report.title: Red Lions Edge Blue Sharks in Extra-Time Classic
report.summary: Red Lions beat Blue Sharks 3-2 after extra time in a match that kept swinging to the final seconds. Fox gave Red Lions the lead in the 28th minute, Gray equalised in the 62nd, Reid restored the advantage in the 95th, Cruz levelled again in the 105th, and Bell’s own goal in the 113th proved decisive. The turning point was Red Lions’ sustained pressure late in extra time, when territorial control and volume finally forced the mistake that settled the match.

sections.text: What a ride for Red Lions supporters: lead, setback, lead again, heartbreak, then relief. Fox, Gray, Reid, Cruz and Bell’s own goal turned the match into a frantic extra-time thriller, and Red Lions somehow found the finish when it mattered most. The last stretch felt like Blue Sharks were hanging on for dear life while Red Lions kept coming.

Red Lions finished with the stronger attacking profile: 4.61 xG to 2.48, 27 shots to 15, 11 shots on target to 7, and 6 big chances to 5. Red Lions also dominated the ball and territory across the match, completing 776 of 838 passes at 93% accuracy, with 85% field tilt and 69% possession; Blue Sharks were limited to 31% possession and 15% field tilt. The last 10 minutes were even more one-sided, with Red Lions at 91% field tilt and 79% possession in a chaotic finish.

Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time in a game that stayed level-headed only briefly. Fox scored in the 28th minute from Lane’s assist, Gray equalised in the 62nd from Frost’s pass, Reid put Red Lions back in front in the 95th from Rook’s assist, Cruz levelled at 105 minutes from Wells’ assist, and Bell’s own goal in the 113th minute settled it. Red Lions had the better of the match overall and pressed hardest at the end, forcing the decisive moment.

fan.title: Red Lions edge a wild extra-time finish
paragraphs: Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time in a match that swung back and forth to the very end. Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute from Lane’s assist, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd, then Reid restored the lead in the 95th with Rook’s pass. Cruz made it 2-2 in the 105th, before Bell’s own goal in the 113th handed Red Lions the decisive goal.

Red Lions were the better side over the full match and especially in the closing stages. They had 27 shots to Blue Sharks’ 15, 11 on target to 7, and 6 big chances to 5. The passing numbers also point to steady control, with Red Lions completing 776 of 838 passes and spending much of the match higher up the pitch.

The turning point came in the extra-time scramble, where Red Lions kept pinning Blue Sharks back and forced the pressure that decided the result. In the last 10 minutes, Red Lions had 91 of the field actions in the final third and 79 of the ball, while Blue Sharks were pushed into survival mode. Reid’s late strike and Bell’s own goal gave Red Lions the edge when the game was at its most chaotic.

analyst.title: Red Lions edge a wild extra-time battle
paragraphs: Red Lions won it 3-2 after extra time in a match that kept swinging all the way to 120+1'. Fox put Red Lions in front in the 28th minute from Lane's assist, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd from Frost's pass, Reid restored the lead at 95' from Rook, Cruz pulled Blue Sharks back at 105' with Wells involved, and Bell's own goal at 113' settled it for Red Lions.

Red Lions controlled most of the game and the numbers back that up: 4.61 to 2.48 in chance quality, 27 shots to 15, and 11 shots on target to 7. They also had 85 field tilt over the match, 69 possession, and 110 final-third entries, while Blue Sharks managed 15 field tilt and 31 entries.

The turning point came in extra time, when Red Lions kept forcing the issue while Blue Sharks were pinned back. The last 10 minutes were chaotic but overwhelmingly Red Lions territory, with 91 field tilt and 79 possession, and that pressure eventually broke Blue Sharks through Bell's own goal.

broadcaster.title: Red Lions Edge It in Extra-Time Classic
paragraphs: Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time, with Fox opening the scoring in the 28th minute from Lane’s assist. Blue Sharks answered through Gray in the 62nd minute, and Reid restored Red Lions’ lead in the 95th minute after Rook set it up.

Blue Sharks refused to go away and Cruz levelled at 105 minutes from Wells’ assist, but Red Lions had the decisive moment in the 113th minute when Bell put the ball into his own net. That proved the turning point in a match that stayed alive until the end.

Red Lions controlled most of the game and especially the closing stages, with far more of the ball, much more territory and a heavy push in the last 10 minutes. Red Lions also created the better chances overall, but Blue Sharks were dangerous enough to keep the scoreline close right through extra time.
